title: Interaction flow capture and action backlog - Feb 2026
body:
Purpose and scope:
Quick capture from 6 moderated usability sessions (cust pilot + internal beta) focused on model route creation, rollout settings, and runtime troubleshooting flows. This is a working synthesis — capture of friction points, concrete micro-interactions that confuse users, and a prioritized list of small-to-medium fixes we can push in the next 2 sprints.

Method:
- Tasks given: create new route (from model catalog), pin model version, configure canary rollout (10% -> 50%), set a fallback model, and inspect a slow request trace.
- Participants: 4 platform engineers (mid-market customers), 2 product leads (internal beta). Sessions remote, screen shared, think-aloud.
- Prototype used: Figma prototype v2.1 (link above).

Top-level themes (raw):
1) Surface-level discoverability: users expected to find "rollout" controls on the route detail page; many looked in settings and then left flow to search docs. Confusion around where canary % is applied (per-route vs per-model).
2) Microcopy mismatch: labels like "bias threshold" and "fallback priority" are overloaded. Several users interpreted "fallback" as an automated model ranking rather than a static configured model.
3) Implicit state: users were unsure when changes were staged vs live. The CTA language ("Apply" vs "Save draft" vs "Deploy") created uncertainty about whether traffic would switch immediately.
4) Troubleshooting surface: request traces are dense; users want a quick header that shows "likely cause" (e.g., KV cache miss, long decode) and a suggested next action ("retry with shorter prompt", "route to smaller model").

Representative quotes (verbatim):
- "I thought deploy meant 'push to prod' — why is this still in the drafts area?"
- "Where is the canary percentage? I would expect a slider on the route page."
- "The trace shows numbers but I don't know what's good or bad here."

Screen-level observations and quick fixes (proto refs in linked_artifacts):
- Route list: add column for active rollout (text + pill). Users scan list to confirm status — currently they open each route. QUICK FIX (small): add "rollout status" column. Ticket: RW-10112.
- Canary config: replace percent input with slider + inline example ("10% = 1 in 10 requests on average"). Also add tooltip: "per-route traffic split" vs "global". Medium: RW-10113 (design + frontend).
- Save/Deploy affordance: change buttons to primary = "Deploy (staged->live)" and secondary = "Save draft"; show small inline status tag after deploy starts ("Deploying: 12% complete"). Medium: RW-10114.
- Fallback model picker: add small help text "Fallback is used when primary model is unavailable or times out" and surface last-update timestamp. Small: RW-10115.
- Trace header: inject a one-line NLP summary computed from trace metrics: "Latency spike likely due to KV cache miss — consider smaller context or enable prefix caching." Spike: RW-10116 (requires infra telemetry mapping).

Backlog grooming (priorities + estimates):
- P0: RW-10112 Route list rollout status column (1 sprint, FE+BE 6d, QA 2d)
- P0: RW-10114 Save/Deploy button relabel + status UI (0.5 sprint, FE 4d, copy 1d)
- P1: RW-10113 Canary slider + inline examples (1 sprint, design 3d, FE 6d)
- P1: RW-10116 Trace header actionable hint (2 sprints; requires telemetry schema change)
- P2: RW-10115 Fallback help text + timestamp (small, 2d)

Edge cases & unresolved questions (capture to discuss with SRE/infra):
- How deterministic is traffic splitting on multi-node clusters? Customers expect true percentages; we need a doc blurb and UI tooltip with explanation. (Open: ask infra for SLI docs)
- If we implement an NLP-generated trace summary, what are the failure modes? Need guardrails and opt-out. (Open: research team to propose thresholds)
- Rollouts layered with dedicated pools: can we show per-pool traffic breakdown? (Open: product + infra feasibility)

Design notes / wireframe tweaks (short):
- Use progressive disclosure for advanced rollout options (weight ramp, rollout windows) — keep initial visible view minimal.
- Microcopy: avoid ambiguous nouns like "fallback" alone; use "fallback model (used on timeout/failure)".
- Pattern: use pill + color for status (green=Stable, amber=Rolling out, red=Failed, gray=Draft). Add accessible aria-labels for each.

Next steps / owners:
- Leah: refine microcopy and update Figma frames (due 2026-03-09)
- Marcus: scope RW-10112 and RW-10114 with engineering (due 2026-03-11)
- Isha: follow up with infra on traffic split determinism and update docs (JIRA RW-10120)
- Tom: prototype trace-summary heuristics and share a short demo in next sync (2026-03-12)

Appendix: session notes (high level bullets) — by participant
- Participant A (platform engineer): expected route list to be the single source of truth; tried to bulk-edit rollout from list (couldn't). Suggest bulk select + apply rollout.
- Participant B (customer): confused by "model pin" and "model version" language; requested an explicit "pin to version" confirmation modal.
- Participant C (internal): liked canary slider but worried about experiments interfering with A/B tests. Asked for experiment tags.

Quick wins we can ship in 1 sprint: rollout status column, relabeled deploy/save buttons, fallback help text. Medium-term (2 sprints): canary slider, trace header summary.

Open invites: drop comments here or ping #console-research-thread on Slack. Planning sync scheduled 2026-03-10 10:00 PT to triage RW tickets and confirm owners.

Notes to self: keep this doc as canonical working capture; when items move to final tickets update linked_artifacts with JIRA links and PRs.
